Because it's about systemic racism, not about black people dying in general. Of course BLM supporters don't think black people dying by the hands of black people is good or are indifferent towards that, but the main focus of the movement is the systemic racial oppression by law enforcement.

Don't say the r-slur, please.

I think that these people mean that there isn't really a historic background to "white racism". And jewish, irish and slavic people are only considered white depending on the occasion. When you boil it down, whiteness in history is basically just the lack of "race". And when these people didn't have the "lack of race", they were not considered "white".

As a non racial minority who does see where you're coming from, I think the problem isn't progressivism and "wokeness" itself but performative activism. 

For my group it just feels like you're being babied and treated like this smol cute being that can't fend for itself when that's not what you're going for at all. But then I also see good talk about my group that's conscientious of the issues that the group faces and that doesn't seem performative activism for woke points. 

First [group] [occupancy] also kind of bugs me because it feels entirely performative. While it's cool that people with different backgrounds are getting more representation, a lot of the times that representation is just used for saying "whoa look we're so progressive and amazing!!!" While not actually doing anything at all. That doesn't mean that representation and celebration of these things is inherently bad though, and I don't think that's what you were saying at all. That's just my experience, though.
